name: VITEM V Work visa (employer-sponsored)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a job offer from a Brazilian-registered employer, who files the sponsorship request with the Ministry of Labour (or Ministry of Justice, depending on the applicable Normative Resolution) justifying why a foreign national was selected for the role.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from a Brazilian employer willing to sponsor the application.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires a documented salary of at least twice the national minimum wage (R$3,242/month, based on the 2026 minimum wage of R$1,621/month).
requirements.fix_path: Negotiate a salary at or above twice the current national minimum wage.

requirements.blocker_text: This is strictly an employer-sponsored status tied to the sponsoring Brazilian entity; it cannot be self-initiated or used for independent/freelance work.
requirements.fix_path: Use br_investor_visa or br_digital_nomad_visa instead if not employed by a single Brazilian sponsor.

evidence_required.document: Employment contract meeting the salary floor
Employer's justification filing with the Ministry of Labour/Justice
Degree or qualification documentation matching the sponsored role

sources.title: Polícia Federal (gov.br/pf) -- Autorização de Residência, the federal police portal listing residence-authorisation categories
Dofmar -- Work Visas Brazil 2026 Guide, citing the 2026 minimum wage of R$1,621/month and the VITEM V's 2x-minimum-wage salary floor
RC Advocacia -- Brazil Work Visa (VITEM V) 2026, confirming the visa cannot be self-initiated and does not cover remote work for foreign employers

notes: HONEST SOURCING GAP on the specific salary multiplier: the 2x-minimum-wage figure and the exact 2026 minimum wage (R$1,621/month, giving R$3,242/month for VITEM V) are corroborated by a single tier-3 source in this research pass; the underlying Normative Resolution setting this specific multiplier was not independently fetched from a gov.br page. The general job-offer/employer-sponsorship mechanics are tier-1 sourced via gov.br/pf. Salary_2x_min_wage in national-variables/BR.json documents the underlying formula reference for reuse across other Brazil routes that may peg to the same minimum-wage base. pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months (48) reflect the general 4-year track; br_mercosur_residency and br_naturalisation document materially faster alternate paths (Mercosur nationals, Portuguese-speaking-country nationals, and several other reduced-residency categories under Lei 13.445/2017 Article 66) that this route's holders would generally prefer if they qualify for them instead of the plain 4-year employment track.
